title: Naturality of explicit open tensor-section comparisons
statement: Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion] and $F$ any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an etale object $v:V\to U$, let $d_v:\Gamma(V,(v\circ j)^*F)\to\Gamma(V,v^*(F|_U))$ be the isomorphism given by $c_{v,j}^{-1}$ followed by $v^*\lambda_F$, evaluated on global sections. Here pullback is the tensor-formula pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], $c$ is the unit-normalized composition comparison and $\rho$ denotes its section restrictions [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial], and $\lambda_F:j^*F\to F|_U$ is the unique left-adjoint comparison intertwining the tensor-pullback and open-restriction adjunction units [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. For every morphism $g:w\to v$ of etale objects over $U$, write $j_!g$ for the same triangle over $X$, obtained by composing its structure arrows with $j$. Then $\rho^F_{j_!g}\,;\,d_w=d_v\,;\,\rho^{F|_U}_g$, where semicolon denotes composition in execution order. No quasi-coherence hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso_assoc to any family of left adjoints of scheme pushforwards. The required pushforward coherence is proved by extensionality: every component on every open and section is the identity. Specialize to the adjunctions chosen by exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction and evaluate the hom at F. This gives c(a,b) at j*F followed by c(a b,j) equal to a* of c(b,j) followed by c(a,b j).

Cancel a* of the isomorphism c(b,j) and then c(a b,j) in that equation. Obtain c(a,b j) followed by c(a b,j) inverse equal to a* of c(b,j) inverse followed by c(a,b) at j*F. Evaluate naturality of the adjunction unit at the top open to obtain section-unit naturality; the preimage-top presheaf transport is the identity.

For a triangle a followed by b equals c, substitute c. Both equality transports in the section restriction become identities. Evaluate the inverse associativity equation at the whole source scheme, and use section-unit naturality for c(b,j) inverse. This proves that the inverse composition comparison intertwines restrictions before changing the coefficient module.

Take a=g.left, b=v.hom, c=w.hom and the triangle equation g.w. Expand the prescribed section component into the inverse composition comparison followed by pullback of the tensor-to-open-restriction comparison lambda_F. Apply the triangle compatibility just proved. Apply coefficient-module naturality of section restrictions to lambda_F, then reassociate. This proves the original public equation with its prescribed components and without quasi-coherence.

theorem etaleOpenTensorSectionsComponent_naturality {X U : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (F : X.Modules) {v w : U.Etale} (g : w ⟶ v) :
    Scheme.Modules.etaleTensorSectionsRestriction F
        ((MorphismProperty.Over.map ⊤ (inferInstance : Etale j)).map g) ≫
      (etaleOpenTensorSectionsComponentIso j F w).hom =
    (etaleOpenTensorSectionsComponentIso j F v).hom ≫
      Scheme.Modules.etaleTensorSectionsRestriction
        ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor j).obj F) g
